newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand c.bank says loan provision rules to stay.
newsitem.headline: Thailand c.bank says loan provision rules to stay.

text.p: Thai banks and finance companies have two years to make increased provisioning for low quality loans, the central bank reaffirmed on Monday.
Financial institutions affected by tougher provisioning requirements announced by the central bank in March have asked for the regulations to be relaxed.
The central bank has so far resisted calls to change, a bank spokeswoman said on Monday.

"They have asked for it all along but two years is the timeframe given, we haven't changed it. I am not sure if we are going to do so or not but at this present time it has not been changed," Bank of Thailand spokeswoman Duangmanee Vrongprathip told Reuters.
"This has been the situation for some time and it remains like that," Duangmanee added.
Speculation the central bank was extending the timeframe for the extra provisioning to five years from two had mounted since the baht was floated last Wednesday, analysts said.

The increased provisioning charges -- 20 percent of sub-standard loans for finance companies and 15 percent of sub-standard loans for banks -- were imposed in March this year as part of a package of measures to increase confidence in the Thai finance sector.
The central bank estimates the increased cost to the industry will be around 50 billion baht ($1.8 billion) over the next two years.
Some financiers have argued the increased provisioning charges are too severe and will adversely affect company performance.
But a circular signed by central bank Governor Rerngchai Marakanond and issued to finance companies on Monday suggests provisioning regulations have been made more flexible.

Though a reserve requirements target at 20 percent of sub-standard assets within the next two years with at least half being made this year remains the central bank may grant exceptions, the statement obtained by Reuters said.

"Thai financial institutions, if they can, are advised to make reserve requirements as soon as possible. This should assist the speediest possible recovery of these institutions ... in following years," the statement said.

"For those institutions which still require more time to make reserve provisions the Bank of Thailand will allow extensions for them and set a provisioning level based upon half year accounts," it added..

Firms which fail to make provisioning requirements of less than 20 percent of sub-standard assets will be prevented from making dividend payments to shareholders on profits unless allowed to do so by the central bank, the statement said.
The Bank of Thailand will not extend the provisioning period for any firm it deems to have inadequate cover for declining asset quality, the statement added.

"For those financial institutions in positions which the central bank believes need immediate rectification, the Bank of Thailand will not give them any reprieve or a longer period in which to make provisions," it said.
"The central bank will inform such institutions of requirements on a case by case basis," it added.
